summary:
SENTRIA is a platform based on IoT designed to monitor the health of astronauts during missions in space. When people experience a prolonged exposure of radiation, isolation, and disrupted sleep, multiple body systems are affected. SENTRIA integrates multiple variables that are analyzed separately. Among them are cardiovascular, sleep, physiological stress, radiation exposure, musculoskeletal, and immune data.
Multiple sensors send data to an ESP32 s3 microcontroller that filters, organizes and shows it via Wifi to a web interface. Using Python, we can standardize datasets that can analyze and use a predictive model to anticipate clinical trends. The system builds an individual baseline for each astronaut with all the variables and triggers alerts when the parameters are away from the baseline proposal.
details:
What it does. SENTRIA is a multimodal health-monitoring system with three layers: (1) sensors and biomedical devices, (2) an ESP32 integration node, and (3) a digital platform for visualization, analysis and alerts.

How it works.

  • Sensors: heart rate and SpO₂, heart rate variability, accelerometer (activity and sleep), body temperature, electrodermal activity, and a radiation detector that generates pulses counted by the ESP32.
  • ESP32 node: receives data, identifies the source sensor, applies initial filtering, timestamps and organizes measurements, and transmits them via Bluetooth/Wi-Fi.
  • Modules: cardiovascular (tracks changes over time per individual), sleep (activity/rest patterns and trends), physiological stress (HRV, temperature, electrodermal response), radiation (temporal exposure), musculoskeletal (bone density history, exercise compliance) and immune/biomarkers (periodic clinical results).
  • Individual baseline: built from pre-flight and in-flight clinical evaluations (glucose, calcium, creatinine, electrolytes, BUN) to detect metabolic deviations.
  • Analysis: a Python environment standardizes public NASA physiological data into structured .csv files and applies bioinformatic algorithms and predictive models for early trend detection.
  • Alerts: flags out-of-range values and worrying trends relative to each astronaut’s baseline (e.g., declining sleep combined with cardiovascular changes).
  • Interface: intuitive dashboard with real-time telemetry and manual upload of lab results.

Benefits and impact. One platform instead of isolated tools; personalized, baseline-driven monitoring; earlier detection of physiological risks; and recommendations on training, nutrition and stress mitigation, which supports crew autonomy on long missions.

Limitations. SENTRIA monitors patterns and trends. It does not replace clinical diagnostic equipment or diagnose psychological state. Radiation measurement would require a dosimeter calibrated for the space environment.

Tools. ESP32, biomedical sensors (heart rate/SpO₂, accelerometer, temperature, electrodermal, radiation detector), Python, CSV data pipelines, [add: web framework/dashboard tool].

Creativity. It integrates physiological, environmental and clinical data into one view and personalizes everything to the individual instead of population averages.
